summary: Alison Denton Jones is a scholar in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She was doctoral student to Martin King Whyte and also studied under Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret H. Dornish.

Alka Patel specializes in history and archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned a bachelor's degree at Mount Holyoke College (~1985–1989) and a PhD at Harvard University (~1993–2000), becoming Associate Professor at UC Irvine around 2007.

Allan G. Grapard (1944–2025) was a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning a Ph.D. from INALCO, he served at the University of California as ISF Professor of Shinto Studies (~1985–2004) and Professor Emeritus at UCSB.

Philosopher Allan Gibbard (born 1942) earned a B.A. from Swarthmore College (~1959–1963) and a Ph.D. from Harvard University (~1965–1971). He taught at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and University of Michigan (1977–2016).
Allan H. Barr is a sinologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford by 1983. In 1981, he joined Pomona College as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures.

Allan Harrison Fry (1910–1979) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Princeton (A.B. ~1928–1932), Basel (1935–1937), and Bonn (1935–1937). He taught at Fordham (~1938–1941), Catholic University of America (1941), and The New School.

Allen Wright Thrasher (born 1946) specializes in Indology and philosophy. He completed his doctorate under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1968–1974) alongside traditional teachers, later serving at the Library of Congress (~1986–2012).
Allison Busch (1969–2020) was an Indology scholar who studied under Sheldon Pollock. She served at Columbia University as Associate Professor of Hindi Literature (attested 2026).
Alnis Dickson works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Dickson completed an MA at McGill University (attested 2009) under supervisor Lara Braitstein and studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Alois Anton Führer (1853–1930) was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned a Ph.D. at Würzburg (1874–1879) under Julius Jolly and Georg Bühler. He served at St. Xavier's College (1881–1884), Lucknow State Museum (1884–1899), and the Archaeological Survey of India (~1885–1898).

Alois Closs (1893–1984) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies, earning doctorates and habilitation at Graz and studying at Vienna. He served as Religionsprofessor at Graz's Akademisches Gymnasium (1921–1941) and librarian at Steiermärkische Landesbibliothek (1941–1958).

Alois Müller (1835–1901) was a linguistics scholar. He held library posts at Vienna University Library (~1869–1901), Palacký University Olomouc (1874–1879), and served as Direktor of Graz University Library in 1879.

Alois Vaníček (1825–1883) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University (1843–1847) and under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. In 1882, he was appointed Professor of Comparative Literature and Sanskrit at Charles University.

Alois Walde (1869–1924) was an Indologist and linguist. After studying at Innsbruck (Ph.D. ~1888–1894) and Leipzig, he served as Professor of Comparative Linguistics at Giessen (1909–1912), Innsbruck (from 1912), and Königsberg (1922–1924).

Aloysius Pieris (1934–2026) studied in India, Rome, Sri Lanka (Ph.D. ~1968–1971), and Tilburg (Th.D. ~1985–1987). In 1974, he founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre, later holding chairs at Washington Theological Union, Union Theological Seminary, and Vanderbilt.

Alphonse François Lacroix (1799–1859) was an active figure in linguistics and religious studies. He served as an agent for the Netherlands Missionary Society (1821), joined the London Missionary Society (1825), and founded the Bhowanipore Missionary Institution in 1851.
Alubomulle Sumanasara (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from approximately 1980 to 1985 under the supervision of Yasuaki Nara.

Alva Noë (born 1964) is a philosopher who studied at Oxford (~1986–1988) and Harvard (~1988–1995). He held faculty posts at UC Santa Cruz (~1996–2003), UC Berkeley (from ~2003), and the City University of New York.

Alvan Clark Eastman (1894–1959) worked in Indology and art history, graduating from Harvard and NYU. He held curatorial posts at Boston MFA and Detroit Institute of Arts, and directed museums in Evansville, Pasadena, Winnipeg, and Brooklyn.

Alvappillai Veluppillai (1936–2015) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics with degrees from Ceylon and Oxford. He taught at Ceylon, Peradeniya, Jaffna, Uppsala (1990–2000), Virginia (2000–2002), and was Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State (2002–2009).
